title: Unveiling the 2025 Porsche 718 Spyder RS Weissach

scenes.headline: Highest Priced 718
scenes.narration: A jaw-dropping $217,545 price tag marks this as the most luxurious car ever produced.

scenes.headline: Dual Exhaust
scenes.narration: The rear diffuser's twin exhausts don't just look good; they optimize exhaust flow for better performance.

scenes.headline: 4.0L Flat-6
scenes.narration: Under the hood, the 4.0L flat-six engine produces an exhilarating 493 horsepower and 331 lb-ft of torque.

scenes.headline: Performance Pedigree
scenes.narration: Inspired by the Cayman GT4 RS, this 718 shares a chassis designed for track and road supremacy.

scenes.headline: Aerodynamic Enhancements
scenes.narration: Carbon fiber air ducts enhance cooling efficiency, a nod to its aerodynamically focused design.

scenes.headline: RWD System
scenes.narration: Power reaches the road through a precise rear-wheel-drive system paired with a 7-speed PDK transmission.

scenes.headline: PCCB Braking
scenes.narration: Behind those gray alloys, Porsche Ceramic Composite Brakes stand ready to tackle any speed.

scenes.headline: Carbon Fiber Hood
scenes.narration: The carbon fiber hood not only reduces weight but adds an aggressive flair.

scenes.headline: Head-to-Head Rival
scenes.narration: Pitted against the 2025 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500's 760 hp, the Spyder RS performs with unmatched finesse.

scenes.headline: Luxury Interior
scenes.narration: Inside, "WEISSACH RS" stitched seats with red accents balance performance and luxury.

scenes.headline: Ownership Decision
scenes.narration: So, do you aim for the distinct blend of German precision and luxury, or is raw American power more your style?

script: A jaw-dropping $217,545 price tag marks this as the most luxurious car ever produced. The rear diffuser's twin exhausts don't just look good; they optimize exhaust flow for better performance. Under the hood, the 4.0L flat-six engine produces an exhilarating 493 horsepower and 331 lb-ft of torque. Inspired by the Cayman GT4 RS, this 718 shares a chassis designed for track and road supremacy. Carbon fiber air ducts enhance cooling efficiency, a nod to its aerodynamically focused design. Power reaches the road through a precise rear-wheel-drive system paired with a 7-speed PDK transmission. Behind those gray alloys, Porsche Ceramic Composite Brakes stand ready to tackle any speed. The carbon fiber hood not only reduces weight but adds an aggressive flair. Pitted against the 2025 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500's 760 hp, the Spyder RS performs with unmatched finesse. Inside, "WEISSACH RS" stitched seats with red accents balance performance and luxury. So, do you aim for the distinct blend of German precision and luxury, or is raw American power more your style?

sections.Highlights: THIS… is a 2025 Porsche 718 Spyder RS Weissach, finished in Guards Red with a black soft top and a black interior. The odometer currently displays approximately 600 miles. This 718 Spyder RS is offered with a clean Carfax vehicle history report. According to the window sticker provided in the gallery, this 718 Spyder RS cost $217,545 new, including over $41,000 in options. A partial list of notable equipment includes the Weissach package, 20-inch forged magnesium wheels, Porsche Ceramic Composite Brakes (PCCB), LED headlights with Porsche Dynamic Light System (PDLS), a Spyder RS soft top, leather and Race-Tex upholstery, power-adjustable heated Adaptive Sport Plus seats, a Guards Red stopwatch dial, a Bose surround sound system, and illuminated carbon-fiber door sill guards. The selling dealer reports no notable modifications. The 718 Spyder RS stands out as the most powerful and extreme Boxster ever made. The main bones are shared with the Cayman GT4 RS, including a 992 GT3-sourced 4.0-liter flat-6 engine and a short-ratio dual-clutch transmission. To top it off, the 718 Boxster Spyder RS is lighter than its fixed-roof sibling and features a bespoke chassis setup, resulting in one of the greatest open-top sports cars of the modern era. Power comes from a 4.0-liter flat-6, rated at about 493 horsepower and 331 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to the rear wheels via a 7-speed PDK dual-clutch automatic transmission.
